question.worked_solution:
Given two $n\times n$ matrices $M$ and $N,$ we have

$$
det(MN)=det(M)\cdot det(N).
$$

In our case, this gives

$$
det(A)=det[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot det[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -3 \\ 6 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

We can compute the required determinants as follows:

- For the first determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion across the $3$rd row.

- For the second determinant, we can compute it using a Laplace expansion down the $2$nd column.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -3 \\ 6 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|\cdot 1(-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 6 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =(2-1)\cdot (8-6) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
